## Part A: basic Operations

A1 Create v as the sequence 5, 10, 15, ..., 50 using seq(). Print its length, sume and mean.
```{r}
v <- seq(5, 50, by=5)
length(v)
sum(v)
mean(v)
```

A2 Create w that repeats the vector c(1, 2, 3) four times, and z that repeats each element of c (1,2, 3) four times. Print both.
```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)
w
z
```

A3 Compute and print: the remainder of 17 divided by 5, the integer division of 17 by 5, 2 to the power of 10, the square root of 144, and pi rounded to 3 decimals.
```{r}
17 %% 5      
17 %/% 5      
2^10          
sqrt(144)    
round(pi, 3)  
```

A4 Given a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8) and b<- c(1,3,5,7), print a + b, a * b the logical comparison a > b, and the dot product sum (a * b) .
```{r}
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)

a + b
a * b
a > b
sum(a * b)
```

A5 Use paste() to produce "Student-1" "Student-2" "Student-3". Then identifying the datatype of 42, 42L, "42", 4li, and TRUE. What are its output?
```{r}
paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-")

class(42)
class(42L)
class("42")
class(411)
class(TRUE)
```
  The paste() function joins the text and numbers to create "Student-1" "Student-2" "Student-3", while the class() calls categorize 42 and 411 as "numeric", 42L as "integer", "42" as "character", and TRUE as "logical".
   
## Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these columns (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F"):
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
students
```

B2 Display the structure, dimensions, colums names, and summary of students.
```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)

```

B3 Add a column average = mean of midterm and final for each student, rounded to 1 decimal.
```{r}
students$average <- round(rowMeans(students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
students
```

B4 Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >= 75.
```{r}
students$passed <- students$average >= 72 & students$attendance >= 75
students
```

B5 Using ifelse(), add a column standing with these values based on average:
* "Honors" if average >= 90
* "Good" if average >= 75 (and below)
* "Needs Support" otherwise
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students
```

B6 Write a function classifying(score) that uses an if/ elde if/ else/ chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 or above, "Merit" for 70 to 84. "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply (c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify) and print the result.
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)

```

## Part C: rbind() and cbind()

C1 Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including
average, passed and standing, computed the same way:

* id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
* id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80

Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all.
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round(rowMeans(new_students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 72 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                         ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all
```

C2 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6). Use cbind() to attach it
to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class().
```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
class(students_all)
students_all
```

C3 Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean".
```{r}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m_with_mean <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m_with_mean
```

C4 In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different
column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()
tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e));
```{r}
bad <- data.frame(id = 11, student_name = "Katy") # Incorrect column name

tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

```
    The rbind() function requires every data frame being combined to have the exact same column names and layout. If there is a mismatch in column names (like student_name instead of name), R won't be able to map the rows together.

Part D: Subsetting

Use students_all (with quiz) for all questions. Print every result.
D1 Extract the name column in three ways: $, [["name"]], and [ , "name"].
```{r}
students_all$name
students_all[["name"]]
students_all[, "name"]
```

D2 Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the columns name, midterm, final.
```{r}
students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```

D3 Using logical subsetting, select students withattendance' above 90.
```{r}
students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
```

D4 Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only
name, section and final.
```{r}
subset(
  students_all,
  sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75,
  select = c("name", "section", "final")
)
```

D5 Use which.max() and which.min() to report the name of the student with the highest and lowest
average.
```{r}
# For the student with the highest average
students_all$name[which.max(students_all$average)]

# For the student with the lowest average
students_all$name[which.min(students_all$average)]
```

D6 Sort students_all by average in descending order, then print the top 3 rows.
```{r}
students_sorted <- students_all[order(-students_all$average), ]
head(students_sorted, 3)
```
